title: Adaptive link-rate smoothing and NCCL pacing for heterogeneous interconnects
author: Priya Kannan
description: Background: On clusters with heterogeneous interconnects (mixed NVLink/NIC link speeds and asymmetrical topologies) we observed recurring NCCL stalls and bandwidth oscillation under TP workloads. This manifested as throughput variance across microbatches and elevated p99 tail latency for short-running inference requests. Motivation: previous fixes focused on static stream priorities or rigid batching heuristics which either underutilize good links or exacerbate stalls on slow links. This PR implements an adaptive link-rate smoothing layer and NCCL pacing integration to harmonize collective launches with per-peer link conditions and the runtime scheduler. Key changes and approach: 1) Link-rate estimator: continuous lightweight probe that measures effective per-peer bandwidth and short-term variability; estimator lives in scheduler/peer-rate-estimator and exports a smoothed rate with decay/window parameters tuned for inference workloads. 2) NCCL pacing adaptor: introduces optional pacing tokens in the comm adapter to space collective launches when peer variability is high; pacing is conservative by default and disabled for uniformly fast topologies. 3) Slack windows & micro-shear prevention: scheduler now computes a small slack window for kernel dispatch to absorb jittered arrival times from peers and aligns kernel launches with KV-cache prefetch completion when available. 4) KV cache alignment hook: prefetch manager negotiates a preferred alignment point with the scheduler for batched requests so comm-heavy windows avoid blocking on cache population. 5) Telemetry & guardrails: new metrics (peer_effective_bw, nccl_pacing_suppressed, pacing_tokens_issued) and a dynamic safety threshold that disables pacing if aggregate throughput would drop. Performance: in lab runs (8-node, mixed NVLink + EDR InfiniBand topology) typical large-TP workloads gained 12-18% sustained throughput and p99 latency improved by ~25% for short requests; NCCL stall events as recorded by tracers dropped ~60%. Testing and validation: - microbench suite: tp_collectives_bench extended with hetero-link scenarios - end-to-end canary: perf-canary harness with 10% traffic for 48h - unit + integration: scheduler, comm adapter, kv prefetch mocks - stress: ramp tests up to 200 concurrent sessions Rollout plan: canary 10% on dedicated clusters for 48h -> 50% -> global. Operator flags: pacing enabled=false by default for existing clusters; enabled=true for targeted clusters requires no code rollback. Risk and mitigation: conservative defaults, auto-disable if pacing causes throughput regression, and manual opt-out available via runtime flags. Related work: this complements prior comm scheduling efforts (see ENG-6123 family) and is intended to pair with future topology-aware kernel selectors. Notes: preserves existing public API surface; only runtime internals and ops docs are updated.
